why: the fallback only sees pre-upgrade rows, whose outcome (ticket-stuck) cannot tell a questions comment from a verdict; a comment already handled before the job existed cannot be that job's answer, and both times come from the same queue clock

why: the fallback covers only rows handled before the floor, by older code, so a new column would never reach them

choice: rejected a created_at check in lib/handoff_check.py
why: after the floor, verdict_heads lists verdicts only, so a reused questions ID is already ignored; the boundary check would add GitHub-vs-box clock skew risk for no new coverage

choice: rows handled before handled_times existed (#401) keep the old behaviour
why: no stored time to compare; NOT EXISTS finds no row, so they count as before

choice: split the stuck-questions regression into a shared setup and two tests: retried handoff 654321 (real verdict) and 123456 (reused questions ID)
why: the reused-ID case fails on main with queued-ci-fix in both upgrade modes and passes with the fix; its later REVISE is rejected-unregistered-verdict by the existing job binding, so it stops at the red-ready assertions
